content.text:
I have what I need. All audit-type rights in this document run **against** the counterparty (Cellco as Servicer/Custodian) and **in favour of** our parties (Issuer/Depositor):

- **§ 3.6 (p0131)** — Servicer must give the Issuer, Depositor, Administrator and Trustees access to its records, capped at once per calendar year on reasonable notice, at the Servicer's offices during business hours.
- **§ 3.4(e) (p0146)** — Custodian (Cellco) gives the Depositor and Issuer access to Receivable Files/systems.
- **Art. XIV / p0444–p0446** — Servicer must grant the Asset Representations Reviewer access to Review Materials.
- **p0437, p1045–p1052** — Regulation AB Compliance Statement, Servicing Assessment, Attestation Report and Annual Certification are all Servicer deliverables to us.

The word "audit" does not appear anywhere in the document, and targeted searches found no reciprocal inspection, verification or records-access right exercisable by Cellco (in any capacity) against the Issuer or Depositor, and no remote/system-access right against our party. The only "access to the Servicer" provision (p0146) is Cellco-to-Cellco (Custodian to Servicer) and does not touch our records.

Since no audit right binds our party, there is nothing to cap — the rule's protective purpose is fully satisfied, so this is compliant rather than "missing" (a missing finding would only apply if the rule expected a clause operating in our favour). No redline is warranted.

input.quote: Section 3.6 Review of Servicer's Records. The Servicer will maintain records and documents relating to its performance under this Agreement according to its customary business practices. Upon reasonable request not more than once during any calendar year, and with reasonable notice, the Servicer will give the Issuer, the Depositor, the Parent Support Provider, the Administrator, the Owner Trustee and the Indenture Trustee (or their representatives) access to the records and documents to conduct a review of the Servicer's performance under this Agreement.
input.rationale: No audit, inspection or verification right binds our party. Every review/access right in the Agreement runs against the counterparty (Cellco as Servicer and as Custodian) and in favour of the Issuer/Depositor: Section 3.6 (p0131) gives us access to the Servicer's records, capped at once per calendar year on reasonable notice, at the Servicer's offices during normal business hours; Section 3.4(e) (p0146) gives the Depositor and Issuer access to the Receivable Files and receivables systems; Article XIV (p0444-p0446) requires the Servicer to grant the Asset Representations Reviewer access to Review Materials; and p0437 plus the Form of Annual Certification (p1045-p1052) impose the Regulation AB Compliance Statement, Servicing Assessment, Attestation Report and annual certification on the Servicer as deliverables to us. The term "audit" does not appear in the document, and targeted searches surfaced no reciprocal right for Cellco in any capacity to inspect the Issuer's or Depositor's records, no unannounced or unlimited review right against us, and no remote access to our systems (the one Custodian-to-Servicer access provision at p0146 is internal to the counterparty's own roles). The rule's protective purpose is therefore satisfied in full at the preferred level, since there is no audit exposure to constrain; this is not a "missing" finding because the rule exists only to cap audits of our party, not to create a right in our favour. Noted for completeness rather than as a deviation: the reviews we do hold under Section 3.6 and 3.4(e) are silent on cost allocation and are subject to the Servicer's confidentiality, privacy and data protection policies, but these are rights benefiting us and are outside the scope of this rule.
